method: Weigh the individual pizza base before cooking, using the raw weight listed in the ingredients. Preheat the oven to the temperature stated on its packet. Put a baking tray inside to heat. Keep the base ready on a board; follow any packet instruction to pre-bake it, and use its stated baking time for the final oven stage.
Slice the mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and cook the peppers for 5–6 minutes until softened; transfer them to a clean bowl.

Check the salmon fillet for pin bones and pat it dry. Keep it as a fillet for cooking. Coat with all the measured paprika, chilli powder and garlic powder. After handling raw salmon fillet, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the salmon over a medium heat for about 4–5 minutes on the first side and 3–4 minutes on the other; start skin-side down if it has skin. Turn with a wide spatula. Check the thickest part: the fish should be opaque through the centre and separate readily into flakes. Keep cooking if the centre is translucent.

Transfer large flakes of the cooked salmon to the bowl of peppers. Add the measured tomato passata to the empty frying pan and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened so it will not soak the base.

Spread all the thickened tomato passata over the individual pizza base, leaving a narrow border. Arrange the cooked peppers and large flakes of the cooked salmon evenly on top. Carefully slide onto the hot tray.
Bake for the pizza base packet's stated time, until the dough is cooked through, the base is crisp underneath and the topping is hot throughout. Rest for one minute, cut and serve.
